    └───────┴─────────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    The env form's post-resume behaviour is unspecified across trials, and wrong in both. A refusal beats either, so I'm rejecting it on measurement rather than taste: codex simply
    has no fact about which pane it's in.

    The boundary that would have fooled me

    codex exec is correct by default — ppid 13636, not the daemon, so it sees its own pane with no flags at all. The entire defect class is invisible to it. My first control
    "passed" and I only caught it by checking the ppid. m6's finding stands because they measured interactive TUIs, but any exec-based verification of this issue proves nothing.

    Design and size

    m6's file-record form, with one addition I'd argue is the load-bearing part: a record that outlives its procodex mis-binds undetectably — nothing inside a codex command
    distinguishes "S in P1" from "S in P2". So fix the lifetime, not the contents: procodex deletes the record when the TUI it launched exits. Then a resume through procodex
    re-mints correctly, and a resume outside it finds no record and is refused — m6's constraint 1 made true rather than intended.

    Size: launcher side 0 against the cap (procodex lives outside fleet/); flock side ~36 core lines (18 read/validate, 12 resolveCaller, 6 seam). Against 4350/4350 that does not
    fit. That's the real blocker on #1572, and I flagged it as the architect's and m6's decision — I won't delete identity rules to make room, having made and reverted that mistake
    once in this PR.

    Two product calls I flagged rather than decided: a codex session resumed outside procodex stops working, and vanilla codex is refused. Both belong in the spec and guide or they
    read as bugs.

    Housekeeping: scratch workspace w1P closed, /tmp/m4meas left for m6 to re-read, shared daemon 17483 untouched — it's 19h old and other agents depend on it, and it's also what
    makes the defect measurable.

    Full write-up: ~/.adaai/flock/m4-codex-identity-measurement-1572.md
